chunks: Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar from Abu Basir who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The fornicator, when he commits fornication, is lashed three times and killed in the fourth, meaning when he is lashed three times.

As for what Yunus narrated from Abu al-Hasan al-Jawid (peace be upon him) saying: The companions of all major sins, when the hadd punishment is established against them, are killed in the third. This does not contradict the first report, for we specify it for what is other than the punishment of fornication, such as drinking wine and other than it, as we will clarify later, God willing.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person who commits a major sin like drinking wine after being lashed three times?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between the punishment for fornication (zina) and other major sins (kaba'ir) like drinking wine, reconciling apparent contradictions in the reports of Imam al-Sadiq. While fornication is punished by lashing, the general rule for other major sins is execution upon the third instance of punishment, a principle rooted in the concept of repeated defiance of divine law. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly approach to differentiating specific hudud rulings from general penal precedents.
